title.value: Preventing Dimensional Collapse in Contrastive Local Learning with Subsampling
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly stated at the beginning of the document, which is typical of academic papers.
title.quote: Preventing Dimensional Collapse in Contrastive Local Learning with Subsampling

extractions.description: This paper investigates the challenge of training Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) via self-supervised objectives, proposing a local learning approach to improve parallelization. The study identifies a phenomenon called dimensional collapse, where information degrades when DNNs are split into distinct blocks for independent updates. To address this, the authors propose a novel blockwise feature-similarity sampling strategy that prevents information loss during local learning. The method's effectiveness is validated through experiments on datasets like CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and STL-10, improving accuracy for models with increased block splits.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving the efficiency and accuracy of training Deep Neural Networks using contrastive local learning. There is no direct mention or focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper presents an investigation of the challenges of training Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) via self-supervised objectives, using local learning as a parallelizable alternative to traditional backpropagation.

primary_category.quote: We focus on approaching the contrastive learning SimCLR framework (Chen et al., 2020), a leading contrastive learning method, through the lens of local learning, owing to its simplicity and widespread use.
